samples.summary:
The feature ships completely unreachable: `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned at 0.7.22 while `supportsClientKey()` requires >= 0.7.23, so every entry point (Settings switch, chip offer, durable client) is gated off and none of the design's Goals are met for any user.

`yorkie-capabilities.ts` sets `MinClientKeyVersion = "0.7.23"`; `packages/frontend/package.json` pins `"@yorkie-js/react": "0.7.22"`. `supportsClientKey()` therefore returns false, which (a) hides the Settings `Offline` section entirely (`app/settings/page.tsx`: `{offlineAvailable && (...)}`), (b) suppresses the chip's `offerOffline` action, and (c) refuses the durable branch in `useDurableDocument`. The stated Goal — "Edits made while disconnected survive a reload ... on a device where the user has asked for it" — cannot be reached by anybody on this branch.

The design doc under review acknowledges this deliberately (§ Rollout: "PR 4 lands inert, and stays inert until one upstream release ... the Goals at the top of this document are unmet until the dependency is bumped"), so this may be the intended dark launch rather than a defect. Raising it because the doc and the spec it defines arrive in the same change, and a reviewer should consciously decide whether ~5,000 lines of untriggerable machinery is the right thing to merge before the dependency bump that activates it — the whole surface will be exercised for the first time by a one-line version change with no code review attached to it.

The design doc names a reuse the implementation does not perform, in two places.

§ Losing work anyway: "we already have the machinery for it in `DocumentCopyService` / `POST /documents/:id/copy`", and the See Also entry: "[document-copy.md](document-copy.md) — the copy engine the offline-copy recovery path reuses".

`lib/offline-copy-recovery.ts` uses none of it. It calls `createWorkspaceDocument` from `@/api/workspaces` plus `applyImportedContent` from `@/app/documents/apply-imported-content` (and, for notes, a hand-rolled Yorkie client in `writeNote`). `copyDocument` / `POST /documents/:id/copy` is never imported. The choice looks right — the copy endpoint duplicates a document the *server* holds, and an archive's content by definition is not on the server — but the doc now records a dependency that does not exist, which is the thing the next reader will plan against. Fold the actual reuse (the import engine) into the doc, or drop the See Also entry.

The store-key parser is written three times, in a module that explicitly exports it to prevent exactly that.

`wafflebase-doc-store.ts:230` exports `documentKeyOf(key)` with the comment: "Defined here because this module is where store keys are consumed, and two copies of the rule is how the guard that matched a lock name against a store key came to be silently false." `durable-session.ts` imports it correctly.

But `offline-copy.ts:53` defines a private `documentIdOf` with the identical body (`split("/")`, take last, fall back to the whole key), and `offline-copy-recovery.ts:146` open-codes the same `split("/")` inside `describeArchivedDocument`. Three copies of one rule about the SDK's key shape, in one feature, against the author's own stated reason for exporting it. If the SDK's key layout ever changes, two of the three will silently stop matching — the precise failure mode the comment describes.

`deleteWorkspace` pays the offline-cleanup cost unconditionally, for users who have never enabled the feature.

`documentIdsIn(id)` runs before the DELETE on every workspace deletion, and it issues two network requests: `fetchWorkspace(ref)` plus an unscoped `fetchDocuments()` (the user's *whole* document listing, then filtered client-side). Neither the preference nor `isOfflineUser()` is consulted first — `purgeOfflineDocuments` only bails on the recorded identity *after* the listing has already happened.

`removeMember` on the very next function gets this right: `const leaving = isOfflineUser(String(userId)); const doomed = leaving ? await documentIdsIn(workspaceId) : [];`. The asymmetry is unexplained.

This contradicts the design's own stated property (§ Client identity: "Keeping the non-persisting path on the ambient client is what makes the opt-in free for everyone who declines it"). The feature currently cannot even be enabled by anyone (see the version-pin finding), so today 100% of workspace deletions pay two extra round trips for cleanup that is guaranteed to purge nothing. Gating on `isOfflineUser()`/the preference the way `removeMember` does costs one line.

The Rollout table plans five PRs (2 = store only "not yet wired", 3 = per-document client "still passing no store, structure only", 4 = wire it + UI, 5 = revise sync-status.md) and gives a reason for the split: "so that a regression in either is unambiguous". This change lands 2, 3, 4 and 5 together as one ~5,000-line diff. The doc's own staging rationale is therefore stated and then not followed in the same commit; either the change should be split or the Rollout section should be updated to describe what actually shipped.

verdict.reason: The described code is genuinely present and accurate: MinClientKeyVersion is "0.7.23" (yorkie-capabilities.ts:24), package.json:66 pins @yorkie-js/react at 0.7.22, that pin is injected as __YORKIE_REACT_VERSION__ (vite.config.ts:414-418), and all three entry points are gated (settings/page.tsx:35,111; sync-status-chip.tsx:97; use-durable-document.ts:128). But it is not blocking under the design-fit rubric. (a) It is the specified behavior: the canonical design doc's Rollout section (offline-local-persistence.md:592-602) and the originating task doc (20260917-offline-wiring-todo.md:37-41, 242-246, with the manual-smoke item at :220-221 explicitly deferred) both state the inert landing as the plan's intended consequence, with the dependency bump as the whole remaining switch; the design's Goals are the multi-PR feature's goals and the Rollout table (:569-575) scopes this PR to wiring. So no acceptance criterion of THIS change is unmet. (b) The gate is technically mandatory rather than a self-justification: at 0.7.22 the clientKey prop does not exist — durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:36-51 casts the provider to reach a prop "whose types predate it" (upstream yorkie-js-sdk#1357) — so opening the gate would key the store randomly and make the chip promise a durability no reload survives, a strictly worse outcome. (c) Design-doc discipline is satisfied: the decision is folded into the canonical subsystem doc, not a parallel one. The residual cost (unexercised machinery pending a one-line bump) stays inside the codebase, i.e. minor under this rubric, and minor never blocks. The finding itself concedes it may be the intended dark launch.
